clue.text: Body of police that represents the Piccadilly Tube network?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nickname for the police force as a whole
second meaning, whimsical: on the London Underground map the Piccadilly line is drawn as a narrow dark-blue stripe

explanation.walkthrough: The Piccadilly line is one of London's Underground (Tube) lines, coloured dark blue on the famous map. The question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the police, seen as the slender barrier between order and chaos, from their blue uniforms.

clue.text: Royal family's impromptu do retainer conceals

indicators.note: what the phrase conceals sits inside it, spanning the word boundaries

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A royal household's spur-of-the-moment party is kept quiet by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the royal family is what the phrase hides.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Fashionable figures the writer's detailed

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I; 's read as 'has' gives I'VE

explanation.surface: A stylish author boasts that their numbers are itemised in depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is thorough and concentrated, going into fine detail.

clue.text: Confusion of woody grass unknown element topped

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a giant grass with woody stems
an unknown in algebra, like x or y
taken as written before losing its head

explanation.surface: Botanists are baffled by a mysterious ingredient in bamboo.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bamboozled means being tricked and perplexed, so the noun is a state of bewilderment.

clue.text: Academic institutions (former) applicable to male or female

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, and the prefix means former

explanation.surface: Universities that once admitted only one sex now welcome everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes clothing, hairstyles or facilities designed for both sexes.

clue.text: Kitchen device imbecile partner ruined initially

parts.note: a lemon is a fool in British slang
a squeeze is an informal word for a boyfriend or girlfriend

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A cook complains that their foolish other half broke the gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ridged kitchen tool for pressing the juice out of citrus fruit.

clue.text: Relative's Indian side dish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal name for a grandmother
second meaning: a soft leavened flatbread served with curry

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining the two meanings; the flatbread is also spelt naan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a family name for a granny and the bread eaten alongside curry.

clue.text: Knowledge test for elite classes

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An exam on general knowledge serves as an entrance hurdle for the upper crust.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born people ranking just below the nobility, a privileged social stratum.

clue.text: Piece of information nowadays withdrawn by corporation

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Anno Domini marks the current era
corporation is old slang for a pot belly

explanation.surface: A firm has stopped releasing a certain fact these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but means a paunch, which is a tum.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or figure, the singular of data.

clue.text: Huge chaps in semi relocating

indicators.note: relocating moves things to new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some enormous blokes are moving house from a semi-detached.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall; here it just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something extremely large in size or degree.

clue.text: Manage rugby session finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A coach finally gets to oversee a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to manage it, a common synonym.

clue.text: Left darkness extremely quickly

explanation.surface: Someone departed at nightfall in a great hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the past of leave, but it means remaining, as in leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success happens suddenly, as if within a single night, so the adverb means very fast.

clue.text: Possible to find out good arrangement of sublease

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written before its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant hopes to discover whether a decent subletting deal is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something guessable can be worked out by conjecture rather than being told.

clue.text: Style of hair right in bubbly character

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the effervescent quality of a sparkling drink

explanation.surface: A lively person shows off a new hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly character' suggests a cheerful person, but it is the fizz of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A frizz is a mass of tight, fuzzy curls, a way the hair can look.

clue.text: Agitated American son seized by FBI agent

indicators.note: something seized by another is held within its grip

parts.note: a Fed is a US federal agent

explanation.surface: A US citizen's boy gets nervous after an arrest by the Bureau.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussed means bothered or worked up, close in sense to flustered.

clue.text: Distrust that Parisian railway

explanation.surface: Someone doubts the reliability of a train line in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To query a claim is to question it or express doubt about it.

clue.text: Country road below zero in winter month

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it
in a down clue, below means coming after in the word

parts.note: the figure looks like the letter

explanation.surface: A road freezes at zero degrees in the depths of winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan is a kingdom in the Middle East bordering Israel and Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Docker, English, travelled with animal doctors westwards

indicators.note: in an across entry west is to the left, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: went on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A dock worker from England went west with some vets.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, the same job as a docker.

clue.text: Odd bits of speech dry

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A dull talk has a few strange passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is the wine term for dry, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Plan church sculpture?

parts.note: sculpture is an example of art, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone proposes commissioning a statue for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart a course is to map it out, so the verb means plan.

clue.text: Boffin's breakfast food? Loaf

parts.note: an egg is one example of breakfast food, hence the question mark
loaf is slang for head, as in 'use your loaf'

explanation.surface: A scientist's morning meal turns out to be bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is Cockney rhyming slang: loaf of bread, head. A boffin is a British word for a scientist or brainy expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an intellectual, the same kind of clever bookish person as a boffin.

clue.text: My half of horse

indicators.note: taking half of a word drops the other half

parts.note: a gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone claims a half-share in a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild interjections expressing astonishment, as in 'My, how you've grown'.

clue.text: Sort of crossing unoccupied zone with female support

indicators.note: an unoccupied space is empty, so the inside is removed and only the edges remain

explanation.surface: A pedestrian crossing in an empty area is held up by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra crossing is the British name for a pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes.

clue.text: Football team's notoriety Len broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer called Len gains infamy when his antics are televised.
explanation.definitionFit: Leyton Orient is a professional football club based in east London.
